note: Scenario switch "exile" (Fallen, not finished; off by default; island games only; on the Workshop page, never the test link). When you lose Syracuse (deposed, driven out by a plot, or the city taken by Carthage) the game does not end: you flee to a refuge with a few loyal men, and plot your way back while someone else rules. The patterns come from Diodorus (Hermocrates' failed return, 13.63 and 13.75; the exiles at Aetna, 14.7 to 14.9; Dion's return, 16.6 to 16.10), quoted in docs/research/exile.md. Every rule and number here is invention.

refuges.name: Aetna
refuges.summary: A mountain fort two days from Syracuse, hard to reach and hard to take. Diodorus calls it "an exceptionally strong fortress" (14.58.2). Open to you only while it is free.

refuges.name: Leontini
refuges.summary: A free town a short march from Syracuse: close enough to strike from, close enough to be found.

refuges.name: Catana
refuges.summary: A free town on the coast below Aetna.

refuges.name: Messana
refuges.summary: The town on the straits, where Hermocrates built ships and hired men for his return (Diodorus 13.63.2).

refuges.name: Rhegium, across the strait
refuges.summary: A Greek city in Italy, off the map. Safe from the ruler's men and quick to forget you, but a strike from there means a crossing that warns the city.

refuges.name: Entella, among the Campanians
refuges.summary: Off the map, in Carthage's country. Polyxenus' advice in 404 was to ride "into the domain of the Carthaginians to the Campanians" (Diodorus 14.8.5), and Campanians dwelt at Entella (14.61.5). Horsemen for hire, cheaply, but the citizens think less of a man who runs to Carthage's hirelings. Only while Syracuse is at peace with Carthage.

patrons.name: Sparta
patrons.promise: Sparta will want ships and men from Syracuse when you rule again.
patrons.text: Sparta sends silver and a captain with a company. It wants a friendly tyrant in Syracuse, as when it sent Aristus "with intent to increase the power of the tyranny" (Diodorus 14.10.2).

patrons.name: a Persian satrap
patrons.text: A Persian satrap's agent pays you a great sum, as Pharnabazus paid Hermocrates in his exile (Diodorus 13.63.2). He asks nothing yet.

patrons.name: Carthage's council
patrons.promise: You promised Carthage peace. When you rule again its anger falls, and the city remembers whose silver brought you home.
patrons.text: Carthage's council pays you silver and lends you hired men, for a promise of peace. Word of it reaches Syracuse.

rulerActs.name: Hunt the exile
rulerActs.text: {Ruler} offers a reward for your head, as the rebels did against you in 404 (Diodorus 14.8.3), and sends men to find you.
rulerActs.why: the ruler hears too much of you: your letters, your hired men, your friends

rulerActs.name: Purge the exile's friends
rulerActs.text: {Ruler} has {friend} seized. Your letters were found.
rulerActs.why: {ruler} searched the houses of men who still speak well of you

rulerActs.name: Court an angry faction
rulerActs.text: {Ruler} courts {faction} with gifts from the treasury.
rulerActs.why: they are {mood} with the ruler, who needs them

rulerActs.name: Take the field
rulerActs.text: {Ruler} marches out against Carthage's army and leaves the Island to the captains.
rulerActs.why: Syracuse is at war, and a ruler who will not fight loses the army

rulerActs.name: Offer the exile terms
rulerActs.text: {Ruler} sends envoys to you at {refuge} with terms.
rulerActs.why: better to have you home and harmless than abroad and plotting, as Dionysius offered the exiles at Aetna (Diodorus 14.9.6)

rulerActs.name: Tighten the grip on the city
rulerActs.text: {Ruler} puts trusted men in the Island and the dockyards.
rulerActs.why: a new ruler secures the strong places first

rulerActs.name: Feed the people
rulerActs.text: {Ruler} gives the people grain and games.
rulerActs.why: nothing more pressing, and the citizens' goodwill is cheap at the price

hunt: Whispers: a stranger at {refuge} asks which house the Syracusan lodges in.
Rumors: men from Syracuse drink in the taverns of {refuge}, and pay too well for news of you.
Named: your hosts at {refuge} name {ruler}'s men, and say they mean to strike soon.

texts.fall: You are not finished. You flee to {refuge} with {followers}. You carry {silver} of silver, and {men} follow you. {Ruler} holds Syracuse now.
texts.fallAlone: You are not finished. You flee to {refuge} alone, with {silver} of silver and {men}. {Ruler} holds Syracuse now.
texts.returned: You come home. {how} Syracuse is yours again.
texts.rulerTaken: {Ruler} is taken alive in the citadel.
texts.carthageOut: The Carthaginian garrison is driven out of the Island.
texts.thrownBack: You are thrown back from the walls. Your hired men scatter, and the city has seen you fail.
texts.killed: You fall in the market place, as Hermocrates did when he tried to come home in 408 (Diodorus 13.75.8). {Ruler} rules Syracuse.
texts.huntKilled: Assassins sent by {ruler} find you at {refuge}. The exile ends, and so do you.
texts.huntWounded: Assassins sent by {ruler} find you at {refuge}. You live, wounded{shield}.
texts.huntFailed: Assassins sent by {ruler} come for you at {refuge}, and your men take them. {Ruler}'s name is on their lips.
texts.decade: The decade ends with you still in exile at {refuge}. {Ruler} holds Syracuse.
texts.settled: You go home to Syracuse as a private man, on {ruler}'s word. You live, and someone else rules.
texts.toCarthage: Carthage takes Syracuse from {ruler}. A Carthaginian garrison holds the Island now.
texts.revolt: Syracuse rises against {old}. {Ruler} rules the city now.
texts.wavering: {Name} grows quiet in exile, and asks what terms the city gives to men who come home.
texts.deserts: {Name} slips away from {refuge} to make peace with {ruler}, and tells what is known of you.
texts.upkeepShort: Your hired men go unpaid, and a company drifts away.
texts.startFallen: The revolt of 404 comes early, and succeeds. The army that rose at Herbessus and the cavalry from Aetna take the Island, and the leader of the exiles rules Syracuse. You take Polyxenus' advice and ride for the Campanians at Entella on your swiftest horse.

startFallen.note: Switch "Begin fallen": the game opens in exile. In the sources the revolt of 404 failed: the Campanians came, and Dionysius held the Island (Diodorus 14.8 to 14.9). Here it succeeds. Invention.

events.name: Terms from the city
events.text: {Ruler}'s envoys come to {refuge}. Come home as a private man, they say, with a pledged word that you will be borne no enmity. Some of those with you have wives and children in the city.
events.why: Dionysius made the same offer to the exiles at Aetna in 404; those who had wives and children in the city took it, and the rest stayed "watching for an opportunity against him" (Diodorus 14.9.6 to 14.9.8)

choices.label: Accept, and go home a private man
Refuse, and pray the gods grant him the same favour
choices.text: You send the envoys home with a curse. Those of your people with families in the city take the offer without you.

events.name: Your friends send for you
events.text: A rider comes to {refuge}: the city is up against {ruler}, and your friends inside will hold a gate for you if you come now.
events.why: Hermocrates' friends sent for him, and he came by night "to the place agreed upon" (Diodorus 13.75.6)

effects.say: The rider goes back with no promise.

events.name: Reported dead
events.text: After the failed attack, {kin} would give out that you died of your wounds. Hermocrates' men did the same for the wounded Dionysius in 408, "in order that they might not be given over to the wrath of the multitude."
events.why: a wounded exile is safer dead in the city's eyes

choices.label: Let them say you are dead

effects.why: they mourn you, and forget you

events.name: A follower asks leave to go home
events.text: {Man} has kin in Syracuse, and asks leave to go home to them under the city's amnesty.
events.why: exile is long, and family waits in the city

choices.label: Let {man} go, and ask for word from inside

effects.why: you kept a follower from family

events.name: The hired men want pay
events.text: The captains of your hired companies come to you together. They were promised pay, and there is none.

choices.label: Promise them the plunder of the tyrant's house

effects.why: the promise is shouted in every tavern

events.name: A captain offers his company
events.text: A captain of hired men, out of work since the peace, offers his company to you at {refuge} for two talents.
events.why: word has spread that you are hiring

effects.say: The captain takes his men elsewhere.

events.name: A Carthaginian at the door
events.text: A Carthaginian merchant calls at your lodging in {refuge}. His masters, he says, would rather see you in Syracuse than {ruler}. He has silver with him.
events.why: Carthage plays one Greek against another

effects.why: word gets out that you took Carthage's silver

events.name: The unburied dead
events.text: Syracusans who fell fighting Carthage lie unburied on the field, and {ruler} has done nothing for them. You could have their bones gathered and carried to the city with honour.
events.why: Hermocrates in exile sent the bones of the dead of Himera to Syracuse, so that his enemy "should fall out with the masses" (Diodorus 13.75.4)

choices.label: Gather the bones and send them home

effects.why: the city quarrels over the burial

choices.label: Leave the dead to the city

effects.say: The bones lie where they fell.
